report.rationale: Bug location: linear.py:3118-3128 in import_adr_batch's preflight loop. When a candidate document is missing (current is None), the code silently appends it to hypothetical without checking if the corresponding witness already exists. An externally deleted version with a surviving witness is tampering, not a normal interruption. Fix: before appending a missing candidate, check whether its partner witness exists in by_id; if the witness exists but the candidate does not, raise TrackerConflictError('version absent, witness present'). This prevents silent recreation of deleted versions while preserving the existing recovery path for transport-interrupted batches (where both version and witness are missing). Test: fake-transport that deletes only the version document of an imported batch (keeping the witness), proving import_adr_batch refuses with zero side effects. Docs: linear-tracker.md line ~220-230, adding the new conflict case to the batch import documentation.

frame.materialize (plugins/foundry/tooling/foundry/frame.py) resolves constrained_by references via an adr_by_key dict built from incoming ADRs by str(index) and title. If an incoming title collides with an existing ADR's title, an existing ADR's ID, or duplicates another incoming title, the resolution silently picks the wrong ADR. The fix adds collision detection in the preflight block (lines 53-71) that checks: (1) each incoming ADR title is not already an existing ADR's title or ID, (2) no two incoming ADRs share a title, and (3) no incoming title equals an existing ADR's stringified index. All six existing frame rejection tests in test_linear_tracker.py already use the same pattern (tracker fixture + monkeypatch + before_issues guard) and serve as the template for new collision-refusal tests.
